chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Bashir al-Dahhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Verily, when a man leaves his home to go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for him, upon leaving his family, with every step he takes, there is forgiveness of his sins. Then he continues to be purified with every step until he arrives at it. When he arrives, Allah speaks to him confidentially and says: 'O My slave! Ask Me and I will give you. Call Me and I will answer you. Seek from Me and I will give you. Ask Me for your need, and I will grant it for you.'
And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) added: 'And it is a right upon Allah to give what was spent (by the pilgrim).'

key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation (implied context of going to the grave)
key_terms.قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him)
key_terms.مَا بَذَلَ: What was spent (financially for the journey/visit)
key_terms.نَاجَاهُ: He spoke to him confidentially / privately

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and divine promises for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh highlights the unique status of Imam al-Husayn’s grave as a locus of divine intimacy, where the physical act of pilgrimage transforms into a spiritual dialogue. This tradition underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt, framing the journey not merely as remembrance but as a direct encounter with God’s generosity. The concluding maxim emphasizes that Allah is bound by His promise to reward the sincere effort of the pilgrim, reinforcing the concept of divine reciprocity in acts of devotion.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. Muḥamamd ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Bashīr Al-Dahhān, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: Verily when a man leaves his family to go to the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.), with every step that he takes, (some of) his sins will be forgiven. Then as he travels (toward Ḥusain (a.s.)) he will become more and more purified. Once he arrives (at the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.)), Allāh will speak to him confidentially and say, “O My slave! Ask Me (for anything) and I will grant it. Call Me, for I will answer you. Desire anything and I will fulfill it and ask Me for any of your needs so that I may grant it.”
Abū ‘Abdillāh (a.s.) added, “And he deserves to be recompensed by Allāh for that which he has spent (during the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.)).”
